sessions.phase_label: Final drawing review and file delivery

requirements.title: 3D Shaft Assembly Model
requirements.definition: Create an accurate editable 3D model of the shaft assembly and its constituent parts from the supplied measurements and clarifications.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers the modeled assembly geometry as a deliverable; mechanical feature decisions, drawing documentation, and export formats remain independently changeable Requirements.

requirements.title: Complete Manufacturing Drawing Set
requirements.definition: Provide a complete set of manufacturing drawings for the assembly and its individual parts.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers completeness of the drawing artifact; numbering, dimensional annotations, visual styling, standards, and file formats can be revised separately.

requirements.title: CAD and Drawing File Formats
requirements.definition: Supply the completed models and drawings in the client-confirmed viewable, exchange, and editable file formats.
requirements.boundary_note: PDF, DWG, STEP, and editable native files are parameters of one delivery-format mechanism rather than separate Requirements; approval and hand-off scheduling are excluded as project process.

requirements.title: Welded Assembly Fabrication Sequence
requirements.definition: Define the manufacturing sequence for POS 1, 2, and 3, including premachining, welding, required final machining, and surfaces that must be finished before welding.
requirements.boundary_note: Manufacturing-order and machining-stage decisions form one coupled fabrication mechanism; detailed shaft, bushing, mandrel, and lug geometry remain separate Requirements.

requirements.title: Main Shaft Geometry
requirements.definition: Define the main shaft stock, bores, thread and bushing-seat geometry, and required inclusion or omission of shaft features.
requirements.boundary_note: Tube size, internal diameter, thread dimensions, bushing-seat width, and shaft feature inclusion are attributes of the main-shaft design; bushing motion and sliding-mandrel features evolve independently.

requirements.title: Bushing Guidance and Retention
requirements.definition: Define the bushing's location, fit, retention, relationship to the piston rod and nut, sliding contact, and retained mounting features.
requirements.boundary_note: Location, clearance, retention, and sliding behavior are tightly coupled aspects of one bushing-guidance mechanism; bushing material is governed by the independent material specification.

requirements.title: Sliding Mandrel Features
requirements.definition: Define the sliding mandrel's piston-end arrangement and required holes, keyway, and related functional geometry.
requirements.boundary_note: The mandrel's holes, keyway, and piston-end details are attributes of one component design and can fail or be corrected independently of the main shaft and bushing mechanism.

requirements.title: Lug and Hole-Axis Orientation
requirements.definition: Represent the specified spatial orientation of the lugs and their hole axes in the assembly.
requirements.boundary_note: Orientation is independently reviewable and changeable; the broader premachining and welding sequence is owned by the fabrication Requirement.

requirements.title: Part Material Specification
requirements.definition: Assign and document the required material grades for the shaft-assembly parts, including the distinct bushing material.
requirements.boundary_note: Material assignments by part are attributes of one material-specification mechanism rather than separate Requirements for each component.

requirements.title: Drawing Standards and Template
requirements.definition: Prepare the drawings in accordance with the applicable usual ČSN/EN conventions, using the supplied company drawing setup as an available reference.
requirements.boundary_note: Standards compliance is the requirement; the Inventor template is treated conservatively as a reference because the client did not clearly mandate that exact template.

requirements.title: Assembly-Based Drawing Numbering
requirements.definition: Number individual drawings consistently with the item numbering used on the assembly.
requirements.boundary_note: Drawing identifiers can be revised independently of drawing completeness, geometry, dimensions, and file formats.

requirements.title: Technical Dimensions and Annotations
requirements.definition: Show accurate manufacturing-relevant dimensions, tolerances, functional dimensions, reference dimensions, and other technical annotations without misleading duplication.
requirements.boundary_note: Individual numeric dimensions, tolerances, and reference labels are attributes of the drawing-annotation mechanism; underlying component geometry remains owned by the corresponding mechanical Requirement.

requirements.title: Drawing Visual Presentation
requirements.definition: Present ordinary drawing views without color while allowing the 3D views to remain colored for readability.
requirements.boundary_note: Color treatment is independently changeable and does not determine drawing completeness, technical annotations, or delivery formats.

unresolved_candidates.description: The client reports supplying clarifications, but the clarification attachment or detailed notes are absent, so additional design Requirements or values cannot be recovered safely.
The freelancer questions the bushing length, but the supplied text does not clearly show a client decision resolving that specific dimension.
A small groove between a thread and bearing surface is discussed, but the supplied text does not identify the affected component reliably enough for safe Requirement routing.
The final value 1.6 and its tolerance field are confirmed, but the source text does not identify the affected feature or annotation.
The client requests minor corrections contained in notes added to the drawings, but those notes are unavailable and cannot be converted into specific Requirement candidates.

source_message.text: Hi, could you review this part? Is it meant to be manufactured as a single solid component, or as a separate ring with four lugs welded onto it? source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Hello [FREELANCER_NAME_002],
I have finally managed to inspect everything and review the drawings you provided.

1\. The main difference, which I had not realized before, is that we must produce premachined parts, weld them together, and carry out the final machining afterward. This applies to POS 1+2+3.

2\. The raw input material for the main shaft is tube 108/28, which will be premachined to provide the locations for POS 2+3.

3\. The previously unclear bushing is installed inside the main shaft. **IMPORTANT**: my notes state this incorrectly—the bushing is not fitted to POS 4 and belongs only in the main shaft. Please select an appropriate clearance between the bushing and shaft.

4\. POS 4 carries the piston/rod end together with the nut. The rod from the control piston, which provides the sliding movement, runs inside the main shaft. This is why the inner dia of 55mm must also be machined following welding.

5\. Cross section C-C on the mainshaft drw. shows that this keyway is to be omitted. Instead, the thread for the M100x2 locking nut needs to be wider, and the space for the main bushing must also be wider (40mm).

6\. Where possible, please number the drawings according to the numbering shown on the assembly.

Please update me on the progress, and [FREELANCER_NAME_003] you!

value_updates.fabrication_sequence: Premachine POS 1, POS 2, and POS 3, weld them together, and perform required final machining after welding.

source_message.speaker: freelancer
source_message.text: Since face 1 is flat, I do not believe it needs a machining allowance. Once welded, this face could not be machined on a lathe and still remain flat. We could, however, add a machining allowance to face 2. Another option would be to leave an allowance on face 1 too, then mill it flat after welding. What is your opinion?

ambiguity.description: The required machining stages and allowances for faces 1 and 2 are unresolved, including whether either face should be machined after welding.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
You are correct: surface 1 should not be machined after welding.
The same applies to surface 2, because machining it would be very difficult. Both surfaces therefore need to be finished before they are welded onto the shaft. Is that acceptable?

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: No. As stated in the message (it is shown incorrectly in the drawings), the bushing sits inside the main shaft, and the rod from the control piston is guided through this bushing.
